en: When talking about AI models and about
neural networks,
it's important to understand the terms
parameters and weights.
And parameters are the numerical values a
model learns during training, while weights
are the most prominent class of learned
parameters. And the 2 words are often used
loosely as synonyms. So you can think of
parameters and weights as kind of the same
thing. Thing here. Both terms matter when
talking about neural networks, like for
example, large language models, which are
neural networks.
Here, the idea is that
during training of such models, we have a
lot of data and we use some of that data as
input and some of that data as the expected
output.
And then we have an algorithm, a computer
program that generates a neural network,
which is just a combination of multiple
layers of numbers, the so-called parameters,
which are connected by those weights.
Those layers simply determine how data
travels through that neural network and
which output is generated. And depending on
which purpose we're building the neural
network for, that simply controls for which
input text, which output text is generated,
for example, which is how a large language
model works.
And that's also why more parameters are
typically better when we're talking about
large language models because that simply
means more layers, more numbers, more
connections, and therefore more nuances that
can be captured.
